title: A Small Change (שינוי קטן)
text: Last year I decided to read one short article in English every day. At first it was difficult, and I had to look up many words. After a few months, something surprising happened: I started to understand the news without translating it in my head. The secret was not talent — it was doing a little, every single day.

questions.question: What did the writer do every day?
What was the 'secret'?

title: The New Neighbor (השכן החדש)
text: A new family moved into the flat next door last month. At first we only said hello in the hall. Then one evening their power went out, so we invited them for dinner. Now we are good friends, and our children play together every weekend. Sometimes the best friendships start by accident.

glossary.example: They moved to a new city.

What is the main message?

title: Working With Music (לעבוד עם מוזיקה)
text: Many people say they work better with music, but the truth is more complicated. Calm music without words can help us focus on simple tasks. However, when the work is difficult and needs deep thinking, silence is often better. The best choice depends on the task and on the person.

questions.question: When can music help, according to the text?
What is better for difficult work?

title: The Lost Wallet (הארנק האבוד)
text: Yesterday I lost my wallet on the train. I felt terrible because it had my money and my cards. But that evening, a stranger called me. He had found the wallet and wanted to return it. Nothing was missing. It reminded me that most people are honest and kind.

questions.question: Where did the writer lose the wallet?
What did the writer learn?

title: Starting a Garden (להקים גינה)
text: When I moved to a house with a small yard, I knew nothing about plants. I started with tomatoes because everyone said they were easy. My first attempt failed completely. But I read, asked questions, and tried again. This summer, for the first time, I ate a salad from my own garden.

questions.question: Why did the writer start with tomatoes?
What happened on the first attempt?

title: The Power of Habit (כוחו של ההרגל)
text: Most of what we do each day is not a real decision but a habit. We brush our teeth, check our phones, and make coffee almost without thinking. This can work for us or against us. The trick is to design good habits so that the easy choice becomes the right one.

questions.question: What is most daily behaviour, according to the text?
questions.explanation: 'not a real decision but a habit'.

questions.question: What is 'the trick'?

title: Volunteering (התנדבות)
text: After I retired, my days felt empty. A friend suggested I volunteer at the local library. At first I only helped sort books, but soon I was reading stories to children. I gained far more than I gave: purpose, friends, and a reason to get up in the morning.

questions.question: Why did the writer start volunteering?
What did the writer gain?

title: Slow Travel (תיירות איטית)
text: Instead of visiting ten cities in a week, more travellers now choose to stay in one place. They rent a flat, shop at the local market, and learn a few words of the language. They see fewer sights, but they understand the place far better. Sometimes less really is more.

questions.question: What do 'slow' travellers do?
What is the trade-off?

title: The Quiet Carriage (קרון השקט)
text: On my morning train there is a 'quiet carriage' where phone calls are not allowed. At first I thought it was silly, but now I look forward to it. For twenty minutes, no one is shouting into a phone, and I can actually think. Small rules can protect something valuable.

questions.question: What is not allowed in the quiet carriage?
How does the writer feel about it now?

title: Learning From a Coach (ללמוד ממאמן)
text: When I started running, I thought I just needed to run more. A coach showed me I was wrong: rest days, good shoes and slow runs mattered as much as hard effort. Sometimes an outside eye sees what we are too close to notice.

questions.question: What did the writer first believe?

questions.explanation: 'an outside eye sees what we... notice'.

title: The Repair Café (בית הקפה לתיקונים)
text: In my town there is a 'repair café' where volunteers help you fix broken things for free. Last month they helped me mend a lamp I almost threw away. Beyond saving money, it felt good to keep something useful instead of buying new.

title: Digital Detox (ניקוי דיגיטלי)
text: Last weekend I tried a 'digital detox' — no phone, no computer for two days. The first hours were strange; I kept reaching for a phone that wasn't there. But by Sunday I felt calmer and slept better. I won't quit technology, but I'll plan these breaks more often.

questions.question: What was the 'digital detox'?
options: No phone or computer for two days
questions.explanation: 'no phone, no computer for two days'.

questions.question: How did the writer feel by Sunday?

title: The Kindness of Strangers (חסד של זרים)
text: When my car broke down on a quiet road at night, I felt completely alone. Within minutes, a passing driver stopped, helped me push the car, and waited until help arrived. We never exchanged names. Small acts like that quietly restore your faith in people.

questions.question: What happened to the writer's car?
questions.explanation: 'my car broke down on a quiet road at night'.

questions.question: What did the stranger do?
questions.explanation: 'helped me push the car, and waited'.

title: The Library Card (כרטיס הספרייה)
text: I hadn't been to a library in years, assuming everything was online. On a rainy afternoon I went in for shelter and left with three books and a card. There's a calm there you can't download — rows of quiet, and the freedom to wander without a screen telling you what to want.

questions.question: Why had the writer stayed away from libraries?
What did the writer value there?

title: Two Minutes Early (שתי דקות מוקדם)
text: A mentor once told me to arrive two minutes early to everything. It sounded trivial, but it changed how people saw me. Being early signals respect for others' time, and it quietly removes the low hum of stress that comes from always rushing.

questions.question: What was the mentor's advice?
What does being early signal?

title: Borrowing, Not Buying (לשאול, לא לקנות)
text: Last year I needed a drill for one small job. Instead of buying one, I borrowed it from a neighbour. That led to a 'tool library' in our street, where people share things they rarely use. We save money and meet each other — two problems solved at once.

questions.question: What did the writer do instead of buying a drill?
What did this lead to?

title: The Long Way Home (הדרך הארוכה הביתה)
text: Most days I take the quick route home, head down, thinking about work. One evening I chose the longer path through the park. I noticed a small bookshop I'd passed a hundred times without seeing. Slowing down, it turns out, is its own kind of arriving.

questions.question: What did the writer usually do on the way home?
options: Take the quick route, thinking of work
questions.explanation: 'the quick route home, head down, thinking about work'.

title: The Power of Small Habits (כוחם של הרגלים קטנים)
text: I used to believe that change required dramatic effort. Then I tried reading just ten pages a day. It felt almost too small to matter, yet over a year it added up to fifteen books. Tiny habits, repeated, quietly reshape a life.

questions.question: What did the writer try?
What was the result over a year?

title: Why I Stopped Watching the News (למה הפסקתי לצפות בחדשות)
text: For years I watched the news every evening, and it left me anxious and tired. I decided to read one good article a week instead. Surprisingly, I missed nothing important — friends still told me what mattered. I feel calmer and, oddly, better informed.

title: A Garden on the Balcony (גינה במרפסת)
text: I live in a small flat with no garden, but I refused to give up on growing things. I filled my balcony with pots of herbs and tomatoes. Caring for them each morning has become a calm ritual. A tiny space, it turns out, is enough.

What grows on the balcony?

title: Volunteering at the Shelter (התנדבות במקלט)
text: Every Saturday I volunteer at an animal shelter. I clean cages, feed the dogs and take them for walks. The work is tiring and sometimes sad, but watching a frightened animal learn to trust again is worth every minute.

title: The Repair Café (בית הקפה לתיקונים)
text: In our town there is a 'repair café' where volunteers fix broken things for free. Instead of throwing away a toaster or a torn coat, you bring it and learn to mend it yourself. It saves money, reduces waste, and brings neighbours together.

title: Saying No Without Guilt (לומר 'לא' בלי אשמה)
text: For years I said yes to everything, afraid of disappointing people. I ended up exhausted and resentful. Learning to say a kind but firm 'no' changed my life. Protecting my time, I discovered, is not selfish — it is necessary.

title: The Joy of a Long Walk (השמחה שבהליכה ארוכה)
text: Whenever a problem feels stuck in my head, I go for a long walk. Something about the steady rhythm loosens my thoughts. Halfway through, the answer often arrives quietly, as if it had been waiting for me to slow down and listen.

questions.question: What does the writer do when a problem feels stuck?

title: Why I Keep a Journal (למה אני כותב יומן)
text: Each night I write a few lines about my day. I am not a great writer, and no one else will read it. Yet putting the day into words helps me notice patterns, let go of small worries, and remember what I might otherwise forget.

questions.question: How often does the writer write?

questions.question: Name one benefit mentioned.

title: Fixing Things Myself (מתקן דברים בעצמי)
text: I used to throw away anything that broke. Then a friend showed me how to watch a short video and try a repair first. I have since fixed a lamp, a chair and a zip. Each small success makes me feel surprisingly capable.

questions.question: What did the writer used to do with broken things?

questions.question: How does fixing things make the writer feel?

title: The Quiet Morning Routine (שגרת הבוקר השקטה)
text: I wake an hour before everyone else. In that quiet time I drink tea, stretch, and plan the day on paper. It is not much, but starting calmly seems to set the tone for everything that follows.

title: Cooking for One (לבשל לאחד)
text: When I started living alone, cooking for just myself felt pointless. Gradually I learned to see it differently: a good meal is a way of caring for yourself. Now I light a candle, plate the food nicely, and enjoy my own company.

title: The Second-Hand Bookshop (חנות הספרים המשומשים)
text: There is an old bookshop near my home where every book has already lived another life. I love finding notes in the margins left by strangers. Buying a used book feels like joining a quiet conversation that began long before me.

title: Walking the Dog at Dawn (מטייל עם הכלב עם שחר)
text: My dog wakes me at five, whether I like it or not. At first I resented those early walks. Now I treasure them: the empty streets, the cool air, the city before it remembers to be busy. He gave me the mornings I never knew I wanted.

questions.question: When does the dog wake the writer?
How does the writer feel about the walks now?

title: Learning an Instrument as an Adult (ללמוד נגינה בגיל מבוגר)
text: I started learning the piano at forty. My fingers are slow and my progress is humbling. But there is a special freedom in being a beginner again, with nothing to prove and everything to discover. I play badly, and I love it.

questions.question: When did the writer start the piano?

title: Turning Off Notifications (לכבות את ההתראות)
text: My phone used to buzz every few minutes, pulling my attention in all directions. One day I turned off almost every notification. The silence was strange at first, then wonderful. I check things when I choose to now — not when a screen demands it.
